subject: arcticOutpost
pitch:
Category: Diorama.
Subject: arctic research outpost.
Style: Firewatch flat colour.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TS module for an arctic research outpost diorama in Firewatch's flat-color style—warm gradient skies, deep teal/purple shadows, simple shapes—featuring snow, ice, a cabin, radio mast, anemometer, and weather station as a static model.

I'm sketching the full diorama contents: fuel drums, sled, snowmobile, flag, antenna dish, tent, glowing windows, all sitting on a roughly 6m-wide snow base with irregular drifts and icy cliff sides. I'm working out how to build the base using a lathed disc with height-based color gradients (icy blue at the bottom, white snow on top, a warm pink tint toward one side for sunset light), keeping the geometry low-poly with limited segments, then layering flattened sphere shapes on top as snow drifts.

For the main cabin I'm planning a rust-orange box structure with a pitched roof made from extruded or rotated box panels dusted with snow, glowing yellow window planes with cross-frame textures, a dark teal door with a lantern, a chimney with stacked low-poly smoke puffs, small foundation posts, and a lattice radio mast with tapered legs, cross braces, guy wires, and a glowing red-white beacon on top, plus a partial-sphere satellite dish.

I'm rounding out the scene with a Stevenson screen box on legs, an anemometer, stacked fuel drums with bands, a sled with crates, a simple snowmobile, a small glowing tent, a flag pole, and some blue ice crystal shards, while skipping unnamed elements like penguins or pine trees to keep things true to the arctic setting. I'm also adding a plank boardwalk path from the cabin door to the mast, with footprints leading along it.

Now I'm planning the textures — window panes, louvers, a flag emblem, a "STATION 7" signboard, crate stencils, and hazard stripes for the drums — plus writing helper functions for boxes and cylinders that place and color parts consistently, and setting a ground reference height so everything sits flush on the base.

Then I'm working out the cabin's layout: positioning it with the door facing +Z, sizing the walls and roof, and figuring out the gable end geometry so the extruded outline sits correctly centered along the x-axis.

The whole roof forms a triangular prism spanning the cabin's length, acting as the attic volume beneath the sloped panels. I'm calculating the roof panel dimensions and slope angle from the gable height and width, then positioning each panel symmetrically on either side of the ridge.

Still computing offsets...

Now I'm defining a custom snow paint function that blends warm and cool tones based on position, using smooth gradients across the x-axis to create a tinted highlight effect on one side of the roof.

For the cabin walls, I'm setting up a plank-pattern paint function that detects which face is visible and divides the surface into vertical plank segments, varying the shading per plank for a wood-grain look.

Now I'm planning the front details: two glowing windows with cross frames and curtain hints, a side window, and a teal door offset to the right, all placed relative to the cabin's wall width.

Next I'm adding a lantern by the door, a dark chimney on the roof with rising smoke icosahedrons shaded grey-pink, a plank porch with steps, a boardwalk extending toward the mast, and positioning the mast itself relative to the cabin's bounds.

Now I'm designing the mast's lattice structure: four tapering legs from a wide base to a narrow top, with horizontal and diagonal braces connecting corner points at each height level to form a tower-like frame.

I'm layering in detail elements—alternating red-orange and cream color bands, a glowing beacon sphere and antenna whips at the top, thin guy wires anchoring the mast to ground stakes, and a yagi-style cross-arm antenna built from a horizontal rod with short perpendicular elements. For the dish, I'm working out how to make a concave satellite dish shape using a partial sphere or lathe geometry so it reads as hollow and open rather than solid.

I'll add a small sphere feed at the end of the rod, then place a ground pole holding the dish with its tilted axis facing up and outward. Next I'm planning the Stevenson screen: four support legs and a louvered white box roughly 0.4x0.4x0.3, using a box geometry with a texture for the louver pattern on the front and sides.

For accessories I'm laying out positions so nothing overlaps: an anemometer on its own pole with cross-arms and small cup hemispheres, a Stevenson screen, a satellite dish, and a mast, each assigned coordinates around the scene radius so they're spaced apart and I still need to place the fuel drums without colliding with the anemometer.

Mounting the anemometer pole on the roof ridge, then placing the drums in a cluster behind the cabin with one lying flat. I'm also positioning the tent and Stevenson screen on the front-left, adjusting coordinates so they don't overlap each other.

For the boardwalk, I'm tracing planks from the porch door forward toward the front yard, then adding faint footprint marks with dark ellipses along the path. I'm also repositioning the snowmobile, sled, satellite dish, and mast so the dish sits further right and clear of the mast.

I'm scattering a few more scene elements—a flagpole near the tent and path, checking distances from center so nothing overlaps too much, and bumping the base radius up to 3.8 to fit everything. Now I'm placing an ice shard cluster off to one side.

Still planning the layout: positioning snow drift ellipsoids around the edge and a signboard reading "STATION 7 / POLAR RES." near the cabin posts. For the base itself, I'm defining a lathe profile with 14 segments and an ice undercut shape at the bottom.

I'm setting up the paint function so side faces get alternating blue ice strata stripes while the top surface gets snow coloring based on the normal direction. For the tent, I'm building a cone geometry with four sides and adding a dark triangular entrance cutout.

I'm realizing the tilted cone face math doesn't line up with a flat entrance plate, so I'm switching approach: building the tent as an extruded gable prism instead, with the triangular cross-section in the z-y plane and thickness along x, then adding a slightly smaller dark triangle at the front end to fake a sunken entrance.

Reorienting the ridge to run along x and extruding the triangle in the x-y plane with thickness along z, placing a glowing orange entrance triangle at the +z face, skipping guy lines and pegs but adding a pole-top sphere. Now I'm starting the snowmobile, planning to build it in local coordinates and manually transform it into place since there's no group helper available.

Actually Euler XYZ order applies the x-rotation last in world space, which isn't right for combining yaw and tilt—I'll switch to quaternions instead, multiplying a yaw quaternion by a tilt quaternion for correct composition. I'm also planning the sled details: crates with stenciled textures, a tarp, and runners made from thin boxes with curved rotated fronts, using an SVG texture for the crate planks and lettering.

For the flag I'll use two textured planes facing opposite directions with a slight offset instead of extruding geometry, giving it a front and back with a snowflake emblem design, and for the drums I'm setting up cylinders with distinct colors and thin band accents positioned around the circumference.

I'm skipping hazard stripe details and label planes to keep things simple, and now settling on a Firewatch-inspired color palette with rust, cream, teal, mustard, orange, dark wood, slate purple, and steel tones to define the scene's materials.

Rounding out the palette with icy blues, white, pink, black, and warm glow/red accents, I'm setting up imports from the builder SDK for noise, smoothstep, mix, and paint utilities, plus a glow kit, and double-checking that the glow import path resolves correctly.

Now I'm scaffolding the build function with a box helper for geometry creation, deciding to keep typing loose with `any` for color/fill parameters since the exact exported type names are uncertain, then starting on a snow paint function that blends warm tones based on position using smoothstep.

Writing wood/wall paint logic...

Working out the wall height and floor placement so the body box sits correctly above sunken foundation posts, plus adding a flattened snow drift skirt around the cabin base. Now extruding the gable shape for the roof end.

Still writing roof geometry...

Working out the normal offset so the panel sits flush with the slope, confirming the rotation angle matches the eave geometry, then sizing the snow cap and ridge cap boxes to overlap properly at the top.

Now I'm placing the front-facing windows and door at the porch wall, designing the window texture with a warm radial glow, dark cross bars for the frame, and curtain details to suggest a cozy interior, then adding teal shutter boxes flanking each window.

Working out the door geometry with inset panel lines, a mustard handle, and a hanging lantern with a glowing cage above it, plus the porch platform and step boxes sized to align with the floor level.

Now I'm adding railing posts along the porch, placing a side window on the +x wall, and figuring out a stone chimney on the roof with brick coloring and a snow cap, calculating where its base meets the sloped roof surface.

Working out smoke puffs drifting from the chimney with soft icosahedron shapes increasing in size as they rise, plus sketching a radio mast with alternating red/cream lattice segments and a concrete footing base.

Adding a beacon light, antenna rods, and a yagi array at the mast top, along with guy wires radiating down to ground stakes and a satellite dish mounted on its own steel pole and base plate.

Now I'm adding a Stevenson screen with louvered box texture, sloped roof, and support legs, plus an anemometer assembly with pole, hub, and three rotated arms for the cups.

For the cups themselves I'm using small sphere geometries colored orange on each arm. Then I'm placing scattered storage drums near the cabin's overhang edge—checking their positions against the base radius so they don't clip—with a few standing upright in different colors and one lying on its side nearby.

Now I'm laying out a tent shape near the cabin, extruding a triangular prism along the x-axis so the ridge runs lengthwise with the entrance facing outward, matching the orientation trick I used for the cabin roof. I'm giving it an orange canvas color, then adding a small triangular entrance flap with a warm glowing interior to suggest a lit tent at night.

For shading, I'm skipping separate snow caps and instead blending the tent's base orange tones using the surface normal, then thinking about adding a small sign post nearby using a couple of thin cylindrical rods.

I'm planning out a wooden sign board with "ARCTIC STATION 7" rendered as texture, positioning it near the entrance, then considering where to place a flag pole and boardwalk planks while checking that they don't overlap with the snowmobile prop.

Now I'm repositioning the snowmobile and dish so they're spaced apart without colliding, then trying out a hitched sled configuration behind the snowmobile to see if it fits within the scene's radius constraints.

I'm also checking placements for the flag pole, tent, and clusters of ice shards to make sure everything stays within bounds and avoids overlap with existing objects.

Still placing drums and dish positions, then shifting to the ice shard geometry — tilted cones with an icy glow — generated procedurally in a loop. For the snow drifts, I'm defining scaled sphere clusters that sink slightly into the surface for a more natural look.

Still placing drift positions...

For footprints, I'm planning dark-blue elliptical discs made from flattened cylinder geometry, rotated flat and scaled down to look like small footprint marks.

Placing the boardwalk planks along the path, then considering a small firewood stack of stacked log cylinders near the cabin's side as an extra detail.

I'll also add an antenna wire running from the mast to the cabin roof with a thin insulator, keeping the ground clear of extra cables for simplicity.

Estimating around 200 parts and 600 lines total, I'm double-checking the helper API parameters—rod creation with limited sides for efficiency, and the lathe function for the base profile starting on-axis.

Now I'm working out the base coloring strategy: blending ice colors with darker purple tones near the bottom using noise and smoothstep, plus snow coverage at the top and overhangs. I'm also starting to define the window texture using an SVG radial gradient.

Writing SVG code...

Building the sled geometry... planks, runners, two crates with the ice texture, a teal tarp, and a hitch rod connecting it to the snowmobile's rear, positioned behind it at a matching 20° yaw offset.

Defining the snowmobile geometry...

Still placing geometry pieces...

Still adding structural pieces...

I'll add scattered ice shards as tilted cones around the base with randomized positions and tilts, plus snow details on the chimney, then finalize the answer.
